C-C0036.answer: Fertilization & nutrient addition probably increases foliar & tissue nutrients (moderate certainty). Across 6 studies: 5 report an increase (Labaj 2014; Pokharel 2016; Schott 2013; +2 more) and 1 a decrease (Thiffault 2006).

C-C0031.answer: Competing vegetation probably decreases tree & seedling growth (moderate certainty). Across 2 studies: 2 report a decrease (Bourgeois 2016; Sharma 2010).

C-C0004.answer: The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of creating or restoring wetlands and marshes on amphibians and reptiles, and the results are mixed (very low certainty). Across 2 studies: 1 reports an increase (Ashpole 2018) and 1 mixed results within the study (Stevens 2002).

C-C0051.answer: Water table level may have no detectable effect on soil carbon (low certainty). Across 1 study: 1 reports no detectable effect (Khadka 2016).

D-Q0011.answer: The evidence is very uncertain about the association between water level minimum and wetland plant assemblage, and no direction can be read from it (very low certainty; associational evidence only). None of the linked claims gives a usable direction.

C-C0006.answer: Canopy shade and light levels may be associated with a higher number of species (low certainty; associational evidence only). Across 1 study: 1 reports a positive association (Gonzales 2010).

C-C0026.answer: The evidence is very uncertain about the association between temperature & climate warming and bare ground, but it points to temperature & climate warming being associated with higher bare ground (very low certainty; associational evidence only). Across 1 study: 1 reports a positive association (González 2014).

D-Q0065.answer: Studies disagree about the effect of fertilization on seedling diameter (low certainty). Across 12 studies: 7 report an increase (Paradis 2012; Pokharel 2016; Rowland 2001; +4 more), 3 no detectable effect (Lemieux 2005; Pinno 2015; Thiffaul 2010) and 2 mixed results within the study (Duchesne 2013; Schott 2013).
